public_rationale: Vogt acknowledged recurring remote assistance, reported as 2–4% of operating time in complex urban environments. His explanation included human confirmations and guidance through difficult situations. That supports Marcus’s ordinary-language description of regular human assistance. It does not establish remote driving, safety-critical dependence, or human intervention every few miles: Vogt expressly distinguished requests from actual human involvement, and many requests resolved automatically.
limitations: Supported for recurring operational assistance; strict necessity for safety is not established.
Very regular remains qualitative, and session duration cannot be converted into intervention frequency.
The statement’s date is reported as November 5; the post’s update gives only a relative time.
Primary-source retrieval failed, so verified contemporaneous news reporting supplies the evidence.
